annotator_1_reasoning: A matrix difference is represented as MatAdd with MatMul(-1, ...) terms, and printers are expected to render that as subtraction, as the scalar Add printers do by folding negative leading coefficients into '-' separators. The matrix printers never got that logic: the str and latex _print_MatMul print the -1 coefficient literally ('(-1)*B', '-1 B') and the str, latex and pretty _print_MatAdd join terms with unconditional ' + ', so A - A*B - B prints as '(-1)*B + (-1)*A*B + A', '-1 B + -1 A B + A' and '-B + -A*B + A' respectively. Because CodePrinter inherits StrPrinter's two methods, the same defect surfaces in ccode, fcode, jscode, julia, octave and rcode wherever a MatAdd parent is printed, e.g. matrix elements '((-1)*B + A)[0]'.

An mi is a token element intended to contain character data, not layout markup, so the resulting MathML is invalid and affected renderers can display the symbol as empty. Plain symbols avoid the problem because their mi contains only text. The three append statements are independently faulty branch endpoints covering subscript-only, superscript-only, and combined-script symbols.

In MathML, <mi> is a token element: its content model is character data, not child elements. Wrapping a layout element inside it produces invalid markup — <mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>2</mi></msub></mi> — which conforming renderers such as Safari display as an empty box, making every symbol whose name carries a subscript or superscript part invisible. A bare name never triggers the bug because the plain branch only puts text inside the <mi>, which is valid, so 'x' renders while 'x2' vanishes.
